title: How I'm creating style kits for consistent ai pixel art generation
author: Rsloth
selftext:
Been making game assets with AI for a while and the big problem was consistency. Each sprite looked fine alone, but next to each other they were obviously inconsistent: Palette drift, shading drift, inconsistent art styles, color palettes etc.

Workflow tips:

**1. A short style brief, describing the look only.** One paragraph describing: Shapes, a named palette with one accent color, how many shading steps and where the light comes from, mood. *Example:*   
  
*"Gritty dark fantasy. Heavy, weathered forms. Cold stone greys, rust browns and tarnished iron, torch amber as the only warm accent. Three to four shading steps, lit from the upper left. Worn, chipped surfaces. Nothing looks new or clean."*

Keep subjects out of the style brief (ie. put “lanterns” in there and every asset gets a lantern), and skip gradients and glow, you just get banding. Shorter is better, don't overstuff the prompt.

**2. One reference image per asset type and size.** Character, item, building, UI, each at the sizes you need for your game. 

**3. Clean references only.** Whatever is wrong in a reference ends up in everything you make after it, this takes some curation work.

**4. Downscale with nearest neighbor.** The model doesn’t always draw at the pixel size you asked for, so a straight resize can give you wobbly outlines and doubled rows. Check it before you move on.

**5. Zoom in, fix by hand.** Clean up any soft outlines, speckles, leftover pixels, mixed pixel sizes, etc.

Even with AI tools managing game assets is a lot of grind, you still have to put in the work!
